Vocabulary · Lesson 12

Daily routines & telling the time

Talk about a normal day from morning to night. Learn the routine chunks — wake up, have breakfast, go to work — and put a clock time after each one: I get up at half past six. She starts work at nine.

≈ 50–60 min routine chunks o'clock · half past · quarter at + time · in the morning 10 interactive tasks
NoticeCompare your day and a coworker's.
DiscoverRead the clock; choose at or in.
BuildMatch times, choose, and build sentences.
UseDescribe your real day with times.

We add -s on the verb for he / she / it: I get up → she gets up, I start → he starts, I have → she has. The present simple lesson drills this fully; here we use it inside routine sentences.

Notice before the rule

Two mornings, side by side

"I get up at 6:30. I take a shower and have breakfast. I go to work at 8:00."
"She gets up at 7:00. She has breakfast at home. She starts work at 9:00."

  • The verbs change a little between the two people. Compare I get up and She gets up. What is added for she?
  • Each action has a clock time. Which small word comes right before every time — 6:30, 8:00, 9:00?
  • How would you read 6:30 out loud? And 9:00? Try both before you read on.

Discovery check — read the clock, then choose

The digital time in brackets tells you exactly how to say it

1seven  (7:00)
2 seven  (7:30)
3 seven  (7:15)
4 eight  (7:45)

The system: reading the clock

For a normal day, four time phrases cover almost everything. Read the minutes first, then the hour:

clockwe saymeaning
8:00eight o'clockexactly on the hour
8:15quarter past eight15 minutes after 8
8:30half past eight30 minutes after 8
8:45quarter to nine15 minutes before 9

For exact minutes, you can also just say the numbers: 8:10 = eight ten, 8:40 = eight forty. To show morning or evening, add a.m. (before noon) or p.m. (after noon): 7:00 a.m., 7:00 p.m.

Meaning check

  • Does quarter to nine mean 9:15? No. To means before, so it is 8:45. Quarter past is after the hour.
  • Is half past six the same as 6:30? Yes. Half past always means thirty minutes after the hour.
  • What about 12:00 in the day? We say noon or twelve o'clock; 12:00 at night is midnight.

The system: routine chunks across the day

Learn these as whole chunks, in the order of a normal day. Keep the little words together:

part of dayroutine chunkexample
early morningwake up · get up · take a showerI wake up at 6:30.
morninghave breakfast · go to work · start workI start work at 9:00.
middayhave lunch · take a breakI have lunch at noon.
afternoon / eveningfinish work · get home · have dinnerI finish work at 5:00.
nightrelax · go to bedI go to bed at 11:00.

Two small words carry the meaning. Use at before a clock time, and in before a part of the day:

at 7:00   ·   at noon   ·   at midnight
in the morning   ·   in the afternoon   ·   in the evening
at night  (this one uses at, not in)

Use at before a clock time or night; use in before the morning / afternoon / evening

Use it in real life

Your morning: Describe your real morning, from waking up to leaving home, with times. I wake up at 6:30. I take a shower and have breakfast. I go to work at 8:00.
What time do you…? Answer the teacher's questions in full sentences. What time do you start work? What time do you have lunch? What time do you get home?
A coworker's day: Describe a coworker or friend using he / she and the -s verb. My coworker Ana starts work at nine. She has lunch at noon and finishes at five.
Weekday vs weekend: Compare two days. On weekdays I get up at six. On weekends I get up at nine and relax in the morning.
Find a common time: The teacher and student each say a daily time; together find an action you both do at the same time. We both have dinner at half past seven.

Reflect

Say the system back

Complete this aloud: “For 7:30 I say ______ seven. For 8:45 I say quarter ______ nine. Before a clock time I use ______; before a part of the day I use ______, but I say ______ night.”

Then say three true sentences about your own day with times, and one sentence about another person using the -s verb.
